name: Refugee Status (Refugee Law 1992, PNDCL 305D)

requirements.blocker_text: Application must be submitted within 14 days of entry into Ghana, through immigration officers, police, or UNHCR; the receiving office forwards it to the Refugee Board within 7 days. The Board (Interior, Foreign Affairs, Immigration, and Police representatives plus a UNHCR observer) must decide within 30 days. Rejected applicants may appeal to the Secretary within 30 days; applicants may remain in the country throughout, with 3 further months allowed if an appeal fails.
requirements.fix_path: Submit an application to an immigration officer, police officer, or UNHCR within 14 days of arrival.

evidence_required.document: In-person appearance before the Refugee Board if requested

sources.title: Ghana Immigration Service (official hosting) -- Refugee Law, 1992 (PNDCL 305D): applications within 14 days of entry via immigration officers/police/UNHCR, forwarded to the Refugee Board within 7 days, decided within 30 days, appealable to the Secretary within 30 days with UNHCR consultation possible; recognized refugees receive identity cards, residence permits, and UN travel documents; entitled to the most favourable treatment accorded foreign nationals for wage-earning employment, free choice of residence and movement within Ghana (subject to ordinary foreigner regulations), equal elementary-education access, and identical benefits extended to family members

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Ghana). Published on tier-1 sourcing -- Ghana Immigration Service directly hosts the operative law's text, a strong sourcing position for a humanitarian route in this dataset (contrast Bangladesh, Pakistan, and India, none of which have a codified domestic asylum law at all; Sudan and Somalia's equivalents were tier-2 NGO/UN-hosted only). STRUCTURAL FEATURE WORTH CONTRASTING DIRECTLY: Ghana's 1992 law grants refugees free choice of residence and freedom of movement within Ghana (subject only to the same regulations that apply to foreigners generally) -- an open model resembling Uganda's, not the encampment/designated-area models seen in Sudan and (to a lesser, exemption-permitting degree) Kenya. One of the oldest domestic refugee laws in this dataset (1992, predating Uganda's 2006 Act and Kenya's original 2006/current 2021 Acts), reflecting Ghana's long history as a relatively stable West African host country for refugees from Liberia, Sierra Leone, Togo, and Côte d'Ivoire during their respective conflicts. work_rights set to 'restricted' rather than 'full' since the source frames the standard as parity with 'foreign nationals generally' for wage employment, not an unconditional open right.
